items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO HIGHER EDUCATION

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to conditions of registration for nonresident pharmacies
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5392

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
conditions of registration for nonresident pharmacies

PURPOSE:  This bill would require the supervising pharmacist in an
out-of-state mail order pharmacy or internet pharmacy to be licensed
by the State of New York. The legislation builds upon present law that
requires out-of-state pharmacies to register with the State. Adding
the supervising pharmacist licensure requirement gives the New York
State Education Department (SED) jurisdiction over individuals who are
directly responsible for prescription drugs that New Yorkers receive
by mail.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Amends subdivision 4 of section 6808-b of the education law
to add a new condition of registration to non-resident pharmacy
establishments, namely that the supervising pharmacist holds a valid
New York State issued license.

Section 2. Provides the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:  As New Yorkers receive more of their prescription
drugs from mail service pharmacies, questions arise about how
effectively state law protects them. Present law requires out-of-state
pharmacies and internet pharmacies to register with the (SED) but it
goes no further. If any disciplinary action is necessary, state
officials must rely on authorities in the state where the pharmacy is
located unless there is an immediate threat to public health., If an
individual consumer suffers harm, present law allows for a delayed
response at best.

Although the out-of-state pharmacy registered with (SED) is expected
to follow the laws of the state in which it is located, our law
specifically requires compliance with New York laws governing
controlled substances,, By requiring the Supervising Pharmacist (SP)
to have a valid NYS license, the state has greater authority to
enforce compliance. This bill remedies the obvious shortfall in the
current law. At this time, mail order and/or internet pharmacies that
ignore the state's quantity limitations on narcotic prescriptions (no
more than a 30 day supply) are nearly beyond the reach of NYS
authorities. As the Health Department fully implements ISTOP later
this year, enacting this legislation into law becomes even more
important. All New York consumers should have equal protection whether
they receive their prescriptions from an in-state pharmacy or an
out-of-state pharmacy.

Requiring the SP to hold a license from the state to which the
pharmacy ships prescription medications is not an new concept. In
fact, Arizona, Arkansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Nebraska and Tennessee
have added this provision to their laws, Pharmacists are frequently
licensed in more than one state. In the case of a mail service
pharmacy, requiring the SP to be licensed in every state to which
medications are shipped makes good public policy sense

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:. New bill


FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None to the State.

EFFECTIVE DATE: Immediately.
